definitions.explanation: A large, solid piece of stone, bigger than a stone ({石|いし}) but part of the natural landscape. Often found in mountains, by the sea, or in rivers.

examples.japanese: {大|おお}きい{岩|いわ}があった。
{岩|いわ}の{上|うえ}に{座|すわ}りました。
{海|うみ}の{近|ちか}くに{岩|いわ}がたくさんあります。
examples.english: There are many rocks near the sea.

examples.japanese: {岩|いわ}に{登|のぼ}るのは{危|あぶ}ないです。
{山|やま}を{歩|ある}いていたら、{大|おお}きな{岩|いわ}が{見|み}えました。その{岩|いわ}の{上|うえ}に{鳥|とり}がいました。
examples.english: While walking in the mountains, I saw a big rock. There was a bird on top of that rock.

notes:
{岩|いわ} refers to large rocks, boulders, or rock formations found in nature—larger than {石|いし} (stone).

SIZE DISTINCTION:
- {石|いし}: stones, pebbles (can be picked up)
- {岩|いわ}: boulders, rock faces (too large to move)

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {岩|いわ}の{上|うえ}: on top of a rock
- {岩|いわ}に{登|のぼ}る: to climb a rock
- {岩場|いわば}: rocky area

COMPOUNDS:
- {岩山|いわやま}: rocky mountain
- {岩肌|いわはだ}: rock face, bare rock surface
- {溶岩|ようがん}: lava
- {岩登|いわのぼ}り: rock climbing

CULTURE:
Rocks hold significance in Japanese gardens ({日本庭園|にほんていえん}), where carefully placed {岩|いわ} represent mountains or islands.
